intro: These three design traditions often share a surface. Compare the pace of a pen stroke, the rotation of a star and the unfurling of a stem.
alt: The figure sits in three different frames based on flowing non-letter brush marks, white and blue geometric stars, and winding carved leaves.

variants.name: Islamic calligraphy
variants.look: Broad and narrow marks imitate the cadence of a pen, without representing words.
variants.history: Islamic calligraphic traditions use scripts including Arabic, Persian and Ottoman Turkish in manuscripts, inscriptions and objects. Actual calligraphy carries language and meaning.
variants.when: Work with a calligrapher when text and letterform should both shape an object.
variants.why: A differentiated pen stroke turns the rhythm of reading into a visual structure.

variants.name: geometric pattern
variants.look: Repeated point stars and polygons interlock across the surface.
variants.history: Geometry appears in many Islamic art traditions, including tiles, carved surfaces and manuscript borders. Straightedge-and-compass constructions can generate repeating layouts.
variants.when: Make a pattern that can extend across a wall or page in every direction.
variants.why: The same rules organize detail at different scales and keep adjoining sections aligned.

source.label: The Met | Islamic art and geometric design

variants.name: arabesque
variants.look: Thin stems spiral and branch into curling leaves around a small portrait.
variants.history: Vegetal motifs developed across centuries and media in Islamic art. An arabesque often combines stylized leaves, tendrils and repeated branching.
variants.when: Fill a band or panel with ornament that feels continuous and alive.
variants.why: The branches make a dense pattern while guiding the eye from one curve to the next.

source.label: The Met | Vegetal patterns in Islamic art

prompt: Make one wide image composed of three separate equal-width vertical artworks side by side with precise splits at thirds, full bleed with no gutters. Reveal three distinctive decorative languages framing a discreet portrait of the fictional office character. Plain badge and mug mark only, no actual text on portrait or frame.. The attached portrait is just a character reference. Our character is a 30-year-old woman with light ash-blonde hair in a neat low bun, black rectangular glasses always visible, tailored charcoal knee-length sheath dress and fitted blazer with an azure pocket square, blue lanyard, little four-color windowpane clip when feasible. She holds a signature white coffee mug. Freeze identity, repeat the subject in every distinct art idiom. Copy no reference card composition or type. No writing, digits, words or labels; no diptych or pastiche. left: Flowing broad ink strokes interweave around central restrained wash silhouette of woman with glasses on ivory paper, calligraphic shapes drawn as abstract non-letter marks inspired by the pacing and thick-and-thin pen movement of Islamic calligraphy.. center: Rigorous interlocking ten-point white and indigo geometric star polygons, no tendrils, the same recognizable woman as a small dark cameo surrounded by latticed star webs.. right: Branching leafy arabesque in warm olive and ochre with continuous serpentine stems across a rich brown carved wood panel, small elliptical cameo portrait of character nested in negative space..
